preflightRecovery.title: B10RAW observations.json
preflightRecovery.why: the census record keeps stdout digests, not stdout; the preflight keeps the first 1200 bytes of each print, which is what makes the print-form findings below checkable without re-running the pinned build

annotationBudget.finding: B9 evidence was lost in run 42729776775 (head 39ee8c9) without any CI failure: the B0-B8 job already emits 50 annotations and GitHub drops the overflow of a check run silently. B10 therefore runs in its own job, whose two recorders cap themselves at 10 chunks each; this job used 11 of 50 and the count markers for both reports were matched before any evidence was trusted.

iccPrintForm.note: the generic TIFF print (SR2) returned exactly the authored profile, the RW2 print returned 202 bytes because Rw2Image::printStructure prints "RW2 IMAGE" before the profile (src/rw2image.cpp:63), the RAF print succeeded but was empty, and the MRW print threw the same kerUnsupportedImageType as its -pS because all -p modes share Image::printStructure (app/actions.cpp:1983-1990).
iccPrintForm.b9AnomalyResolved: this also explains B9's ORF 202-byte -pC print for a 192-byte profile: OrfImage::printStructure prints "ORF IMAGE" first (src/orfimage.cpp:55). B9 recorded that difference as undiagnosed; it is a print-form banner, not a profile difference. B9's rows are not rewritten.

recognition.note: MRW is claimed by \0MRM ahead of the TIFF entry, RW2 by magic 0x0055 which the generic TIFF check rejects, RAF by the FUJIFILM header, and SR2 by nothing: it dispatches to the generic TIFF reader because the pinned registry has no SR2 entry, so its rows record generic behaviour rather than an SR2 identity.

checkoutPolicy.requirement: the digests in this receipt are taken over committed bytes, so a checkout that rewrites line endings invalidates them
checkoutPolicy.windowsRunnerDefault: core.autocrlf=true converts LF text to CRLF at checkout
checkoutPolicy.finding: net8.0/net10.0 windows-latest failed the discovery suite at 4322b70 (run 42744015517) while every Linux and macOS job passed: the B10 evidence files had been written without an eol pin, so the Windows checkout hashed CRLF bytes against an LF-recorded digest. Reproduced locally with `git -c core.autocrlf=true checkout-index`, fixed by the pin, and guarded by test_files_whose_bytes_a_receipt_hashes_are_eol_pinned so no later batch can forget it.
